analysis.one_liner: Bajaj Auto makes and exports two-wheelers and three-wheelers (Pulsar, Dominar, CT/Platina, Chetak electric scooters, auto-rickshaws) and holds a 74.9% majority stake in Austria's KTM through its Pierer Mobility structure.
analysis.whats_happening: Bajaj Auto reported Q2 FY27 (July-Sept 2026) results on 27 October 2026, just three days before this close. Standalone net profit rose 35% YoY to ₹3,353-3,354 crore and revenue crossed ₹20,000 crore for the first time (+34% YoY); consolidated profit jumped 62% to ₹3,436 crore. The company credited record exports and the Chetak electric scooter range, whose volumes more than doubled YoY to roughly 200,000 units and which turned margin-accretive this quarter. Bajaj is also reportedly scouting locations for a sixth manufacturing plant to meet premium-bike and EV demand.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a motorcycle and scooter maker that sells heavily overseas and is now betting big on electric scooters (Chetak) and a European motorcycle brand (KTM) it took control of. The quarter just reported was genuinely strong — profit and margins both rose, and the electric business stopped losing money and started adding to it. The tension: despite that strong print, the stock is still 16% below its September 2026 high and has badly lagged its closest peer, TVS Motor, over three and five years, so the market isn't simply rewarding good results — it's weighing whether the EV and KTM turnaround can repeat quarter after quarter.
analysis.quarters: EBITDA margin has moved up steadily: about 19.7% in Q1 FY26, 20.5% in Q2 FY26 (July-Sept 2025), and 20.9% in the just-reported Q2 FY27 (July-Sept 2026) — a genuine, if modest, margin expansion rather than a one-off. The headline jump in consolidated profit (+62%) is noticeably larger than standalone profit growth (+35%) because KTM/Pierer Mobility, which had been loss-making for several quarters, only reached EBITDA breakeven in Q1 FY27 — so some of that consolidated jump is a low-base effect from a subsidiary moving from losses to small profits, not purely core-business momentum. Management flagged continuing input-cost inflation even as the EV mix helps offset it.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is up 17.6% over 1 year, comfortably beating the Nifty's -10.9%, but that masks weaker long-run standing: 3-year returns of 104% and 5-year returns of 211% trail peer TVS Motor's 167% and 539% by a wide margin. The stock is currently 16.3% below its September 2026 peak of ₹12,361. There's no demerger or spin-off in the corporate-action history to explain this away — the only recorded action is a 2010 2-for-1 split, which is already reflected in these return figures — so the current drawdown is a genuine price pullback, not a chart artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E estimates cluster in the high-20s (sources range roughly 22x-28x depending on the date and price used), against ROE and ROCE both near 28.7% for FY26 (up from 22.9% ROE in FY25). The premium multiple is being paid for a specific story — EV mix turning margin-accretive and KTM returning to breakeven — rather than for the base two-wheeler business alone. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether the EV/KTM turnaround proves durable over several more quarters; this report does not take a view on whether the stock is cheap or expensive at today's price.
analysis.growth_read: This was a quarter of both volume and margin growth together — revenue grew 34% YoY on higher export units and more than doubled Chetak volumes, while EBITDA margin still expanded 40 basis points to 20.9%. Electric vehicles now account for roughly 35% of domestic revenue, so growth is increasingly powered by a genuine product-mix shift (EVs) rather than just cyclical demand, which is a more durable growth driver than a pure volume upcycle.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into cash at the standalone level: surplus cash of ₹18,137 crore as of March 2026 and free cash flow above ₹8,000 crore for FY26, with dividend plus buyback for the year totalling close to 100% of standalone PAT. The real risk sits elsewhere — KTM/Pierer Mobility carries its own debt (a €550 million refinancing arranged in February 2026) and only just turned EBITDA-breakeven after multiple loss-making quarters, so financial risk is concentrated in that subsidiary, not the debt-free parent. For the core Bajaj business, the bigger question is business risk — can the EV ramp and export momentum keep up — rather than balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Bajaj family, largely via Bajaj Holdings) hold roughly 55-56% as of mid-to-late 2026, with pledging effectively negligible at about 0.01% — no leverage-driven promoter stress here. FIIs hold a comparatively small ~3%, DIIs about 13%, and public shareholders roughly 9-10%. There is no single marquee outside investor name standing out on the register; this is a promoter-dominated, institutionally under-owned stock relative to its peers.
strengths: Consolidated profit up 62% YoY to ₹3,436 crore and standalone profit up 35% to ₹3,354 crore on record quarterly revenue of ₹20,003 crore.
EBITDA margin expanded to 20.9% (+40 bps YoY) even with cost inflation, showing pricing/mix discipline.
Chetak electric scooter volumes more than doubled YoY to roughly 200,000 units and the EV portfolio turned margin-accretive, now ~35% of domestic revenue.
Standalone net cash of ₹18,137 crore (March 2026) and free cash flow over ₹8,000 crore for FY26, funding a near-100% PAT payout via dividend and buyback.
watchpoints: Stock is still 16.3% below its September 2026 peak of ₹12,361 despite the strong quarter, at a trailing P/E in the high-20s — leaves limited room for execution slips.

KTM/Pierer Mobility only reached EBITDA breakeven in Q1 FY27 after several loss-making quarters and carries its own €550 million refinancing — sustainability is unproven over just one or two quarters.
3-year (104%) and 5-year (211%) stock returns have lagged peer TVS Motor (167%, 539%) by a wide margin, raising the question of relative positioning within the two-wheeler pack.
Management itself flagged continuing input-cost inflation pressure, meaning margin gains are being made against a cost headwind, not in its absence.
analysis.one_thing: Whether the EBITDA margin gain and Chetak/KTM profitability hold for two or three more consecutive quarters, rather than being a single strong print — that distinguishes a structural EV/export-led re-rating from a low-base, one-off bounce.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 results figures (revenue ₹20,003 crore, standalone PAT ₹3,353-3,354 crore, EBITDA margin 20.9%) were cross-checked across Forbes India, Business Today, Business Standard and other outlets and are consistent. FY26 full-year cash/dividend figures and the 74.9% KTM stake are corroborated by company press releases and multiple reports. Valuation ratios (P/E 22x-28x depending on source/date) and promoter holding (55.01%-55.95% across sources) showed minor divergence, likely timing differences; no single figure was treated as authoritative beyond noting the range. Could not independently verify a specific upcoming record date beyond the already-paid May 2026 dividend — check Screener/BSE for the next AGM/dividend schedule.
